summary: NYC DOE opposes the elimination of the E-Rate program and urges the Commission to preserve E-Rate’s core purpose while modernizing the program to meet schools’ evolving connectivity needs. Broadband availability should not be viewed as evidence that E-Rate has fulfilled its connectivity mission and that the E-rate program is no longer necessary. NYC DOE recommends retaining support for both Category One and Category Two services. The NYC DOE argues against conditionally funding E-Rate on federal screen-time standards, emphasizing the need for local educational authority and federal prohibition on federal oversight of education. The NYC DOE urges the FCC to preserve E-Rate support, retain objective measures of economic need, avoid reductions based on urban status, and preserve flexibility under CIPA.
